reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset, and Brown attribute Judges 1:19's setback to Judah's want of faith rather than any limit on God's power, which remained sufficient in the valley.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells, Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Can God stop iron chariots?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/iron.html) (2013).

sides.snippet: Is anything too hard for Yahweh?
sides.verseText: Is anything too hard for Yahweh? At the set time I will return to you, when the season comes round, and Sarah will have a son.\"

sides.snippet: he could not drive out the inhabitants of the valley, because they had chariots of iron
sides.verseText: Yahweh was with Judah; and drove out [the inhabitants of] the hill-country; for he could not drive out the inhabitants of the valley, because they had chariots of iron.
